chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Marwan said:

I saw Yunus in Mina asking Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man when the obligatory prayer comes upon him while he is in the Ka'ba and he is unable to exit the Ka'ba, so he said: 'He lies on his back and prays by gesture.'
And he mentioned the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So wherever you turn, there is the face of Allah.'

key_terms.فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَّ وَجْهُ اللَّ: So wherever you turn, there is the face of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who cannot exit the Ka'ba when the obligatory prayer time begins?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of ritual prayer (Salat) within the sacred precincts, specifically addressing the practical dilemma of a pilgrim trapped in the Ka'ba during prayer time. By citing the verse 'Wherever you turn, there is the face of God,' the Imam underscores the principle of *I'ma'* (prayer by gesture) when physical prostration is impossible, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (*Yusr*) in religious obligations. This ruling is particularly significant in the context of Hajj rituals, where spatial constraints often intersect with fixed prayer times.
